objective: Derive root-faithful bridge gluing, structural conditions on a vertex-minimal counterexample, and an explicit equivalence with connected simple cubic graphs after the fixed-coloring route fails.

atomic_claims.text: Two star-colored augmented bridge shores with a common stub color glue exactly when their alternating arm lengths sum to at most four for every other color.
For at least five colors, a whole-shore palette permutation always supplies this bridge compatibility; the four-color analogue fails for an explicit pair of star-colored trees.
The bridge construction gives an inductive existential star five-edge-coloring of every subcubic forest.
A vertex-minimal root counterexample is connected, has only pendant bridges, and has a 2-connected leaf-deleted core with explicitly distinguished degree-two vertex types.
Iterated deficient-vertex doubling gives a simple cubic completion and proves equivalence of the root with its connected simple cubic restriction.
The generator checks all 27225 five-color and 93636 six-color signature pairs, and every labeled subcubic graph of orders one through five for the completion construction.

assumptions: Finite simple undirected subcubic graphs; star coloring forbids bichromatic simple four-edge paths and four-cycles.
Bridge gluing starts from star colorings of both shores augmented by a pendant stub.
The minimum-counterexample conclusions are conditional on existence and minimum vertex order among all subcubic counterexamples.
Only finite-graph-basic and finite-combinatorics; no fixed-coloring or bounded-edit premise is added to the root.
risks: The gluing lemma does not accept arbitrary bare-shore colorings without stubs.
A same-order augmented shore cannot be colored by the minimality hypothesis; leaves are not excluded.
Cubic completion is not claimed bridgeless, nor is a minimum subcubic counterexample claimed cubic.
Original degree-two vertices and leaf-support vertices must remain distinguished in the core.
Finite generator-side audits are not trusted mathematical receipts or universal coloring searches.
The admitted DAG remains unchanged; these reductions do not close its root.
